{{distinguish|Tate module}}
In mathematics, a '''Hodge–Tate module''' is an analogue of a [[Hodge structure]] over [[p-adic field]]s. {{harvs|txt|last=Serre|year=1967}} introduced and named Hodge–Tate structures using the results of {{harvs|txt|last=Tate|authorlink=John Tate (mathematician)|year=1967}} on [[p-divisible group]]s.

==Definition==

Suppose that ''G'' is the [[absolute Galois group]] of a ''p''-adic field ''K''. Then ''G'' has a canonical [[cyclotomic character]] χ given by its action on the ''p''th power [[root of unity|roots of unity]]. Let ''C'' be the completion of the [[algebraic closure]] of ''K''. Then a finite-dimensional [[vector space]] over ''C'' with a semi-linear action of the [[Galois group]] ''G'' is said to be of '''Hodge–Tate type''' if it is generated by the eigenvectors of integral powers of χ.
